title: Tensor product with a constant complex
statement:
Let $X$ be a
quasi-compact and
quasi-separated scheme with $\kuncd(X)<\infty$ and let $\Lambda$ be
a torsion ring. For $E\in D(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$ and
$K\in D(\Lambda)$, the canonical map

$$
\RGamma(X_{\Et},E)\kunotimes{\Lambda}K\longrightarrow
\RGamma\bigl(X_{\Et},E\kunotimes{\Lambda}\underline{K}\bigr)
$$

is an isomorphism.

proof.text: Choose a natural bound from the defining infimum of torsion etale cohomological dimension. A positive integer annihilating Lambda annihilates every section of each Lambda-module sheaf. Its underlying abelian sheaf is therefore torsion. The source etaleModuleCohomology_forgetIso identifies the underlying module-valued cohomology with abelian-sheaf cohomology, transferring the vanishing bound to HasFiniteCohomologicalDimension Lambda X. Integer degrees greater than the nonnegative bound are natural degrees.

proof.text: Use exactly derivedConstantGlobalSectionsAdjunction and leftDerivedTensorComparison from the defining constant projection map. The constant-sheaf functor is exact, additive, strong monoidal, flat preserving and a left adjoint. Its total left derived functor is canonically isomorphic to its termwise derived functor, hence has compatible shifts and is triangulated; the right adjoint receives the adjoint shift structure and is triangulated. On a functorial flat resolution P both P and its constant image are K-flat. The characterizing tensor/counit square for leftDerivedTensorComparison and the source commShift_of_tensorLeft_fac prove compatibility with shifts at Qh(P). Naturality and the isomorphism K -> Qh(P) transport this to every first input. ProjectionMapShift then proves shift compatibility of the actual counit mate, without changing models to a ringed-site projection map. The proof handles shift and unit data with the coefficient category abstract before invoking module generation, avoiding premature specialization of derived structures. cachedDerivedTensorComparison_eq identifies the compact comparison interface with the source comparison whenever its representative equations are used.

proof.text: Closedness makes tensor-left functors left adjoints in both derived categories. Derived constants preserve coproducts as a left adjoint, and Step 2 supplies preservation by derived global sections. Construct the unit comparison explicitly as LF of the Qh unit, the derived counit at the homotopy tensor unit, Qh of the ordinary homotopy-functor unit, and the inverse Qh unit. All factors are invertible. The source oplax_right_unitality_of_lax_square gives its right-unit law on a common K-flat representative; oplax_right_unitality_of_iso transports this to every input. The general rightAdjointProjectionMap_rightUnitality identity and cancellation of the invertible unit factors prove invertibility of the projection component at the tensor unit.

source.place: Tag 0F12, proof; Tag 0F11 for coproduct preservation and Tag 09PB for derived-module free generation

proof.text: Let P(K) assert that the projection component at K is an isomorphism. The single rank-one free module is isomorphic to the tensor unit, including the harmless ULift in derivedModuleFreeGeneration, so P holds on every shift of that generator. Mathlib isIso_app_coconePt_of_preservesColimit gives coproduct closure. The source third-isomorphism lemma for shift-compatible natural transformations between triangulated functors gives triangle closure; naturality gives retract closure. Apply derivedModuleFreeGeneration to conclude P(K) for every unbounded complex.
